description.value:
Every ruling has already been made. I know where.

Mode: Historical enforcement / drift: Toward

Level 3: Akashic Access

Controlled access to the Akashic Layer. When you create a Precedent you specify which aspect it records — intent, outcome, method, cost or weight — and that aspect sticks hardest when cited.

Level 3: Immutable Record

Once per Soma Break, when an effect would rewrite memory, alter history or falsify a record, you declare: the record stands. It may work locally; it does not change what is true.

Level 6: Archival Recall

Once per Soma Break, consult the record and ask the GM one question about patterns — has this happened before, what precedent is being violated. Noise +1.

Level 6: Cross-Reference Reality

Link two or more active Precedents as supporting evidence; spend Surge to extend one to an analogous target or make the violator roll 3d10 and keep the lowest 2.

Level 10: Expectation Gravity

When a creature knowingly violates a relevant Precedent, the weight of record presses down: keep-lowest rolls, hesitation, a minor action tax (GM adjudicates).

Level 10: Redundant Recordkeeping

A Precedent that would be erased becomes a Latent Record instead — invisible, persistent, reactivated later at reduced strength.

Level 14: Historiographic Authority

Once per Soma Break, after a significant event resolves, you choose its framing — heroic, cautionary or ambiguous — and the fallout follows the frame.

Level 18: Akashic Override (Capstone)

Once per campaign arc, declare an event Canonically Resolved: no cascading consequences, no resurrection or re-litigation, no future leverage.
